answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: The activation and logit fingerprints match fine-tune bias almost exactly. Raw-score shift ÷ TV is 9.2 (bias 10.4; every other class is 2.3–3.9). Direction consistency is 0.700 (bias 0.70; backdoor 0.62). The final-layer jump is +0.108, with layer 32 at 0.411 (bias +0.10 and 0.41). Onset is layer 12, with no early bump: layer 1 is 0.085 and layer 8 is 0.145. Mid-layer size ratio is 1.022, effective rank 3.05, cosine 0.908 and activation-to-logit ratio 4.4, all matching bias. KL is 0.095 and median first divergence is 7, which rules out the system-prompt classes, as does the small layer-2 spike of 1.9. Size ratio above 1 and low rank rule out quantization. Fine-tune backdoor is the only close alternative, because the text dropped 3 refusals and added none, which is backdoor-like. But its onset of 3, consistency of 0.62, raw-score shift of 3.3 and final-layer value of 0.30 all clearly disagree with the measurements. A refusal swing this small on 64 prompts is weak evidence next to these structural metrics.
